title: Real-time model availability scout and operational triggerbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a lightweight, operationally-actionable system and playbook for detecting, scoring, and responding to emergent model availability and pricing events in near real-time. The scout aggregates signals from public provider status pages, API latency/error-rate probes, synthetic RAG and embedding workloads, pricing telemetry (where available), and third-party scraping to generate a ranked feed of 'availability incidents' with recommended fallback actions and cost/latency tradeoffs. Deliverables: signal ingestion spec, scoring rules, alerting thresholds, routing fallback matrix, on-call runbook, and a short experiment to validate end-to-end detection -> routing -> customer-impact measurement.
acceptance_criteria: Signal ingestion: at least 5 distinct signal sources (status pages, synthetic latency probes, embedding probe, pricing crawler, social/incident feed) are producing measurable metrics into the scout pipeline
Scoring: incidents are assigned a severity (low/medium/high) and contributor tags (latency, errors, quota) with traceable provenance

Automated triggers: high-severity incidents create a routing suggestion that can be consumed by the smart routing service (via webhook) and by on-call (via PagerDuty test integration), with simulated fallback executed in staging
Runbook: a single-page on-call playbook exists describing investigation steps, immediate mitigations, communication templates, and rollback criteria
Metrics: we capture customer-facing SLO delta (p50/p95 latency, error rate) and cost delta for any simulated fallback within the experiment window
notes: Scope: MVP limited to top-6 model providers and Redwood-hosted variants; exclude private customer deployments for MVP
Signal design: weight fresh synthetic probe failures and provider-reported outages more heavily than social signals; add rate-limiting to avoid noisy alerts
Privacy/compliance: only scrape public metadata; do not log customer request payloads into this system
Experiment plan: run A/B probing using low-volume synthetic traffic to measure blind-fallback accuracy and false-positive rate
Success metrics: incident detection precision > 80% and false positive rate < 10% during 30-day validation
